description:
First, isolated, fully-tested brick. No producer/consumer wiring yet — exercised only by its own unit tests so the tree stays green with zero dead-code warnings. ## Change Add `ReturnDemandMap

` to semantic.rs, a structural clone of `ActivationInputMap

` (semantic.rs:430-668): per-key `contributors: HashMap` + `joined: RuntimeDemand`, `output_keys: HashMap>`, with `conclude` (replacing arm) and `extend` (blocked-publisher arm). Key = `ExecutableKey`, value = `RuntimeDemand`. ## Why `ReturnDemand(E)` is the backward dual of activation inputs: many publishers (callers), joined by lattice lub, revision bumps only when the join moves. The join op is `RuntimeDemand::join_assign` (semantic.rs:288) — the lattice already exists and is documented-monotone. The conclude/extend split is load-bearing: a blocked publisher must EXTEND (recant nothing), exactly as analyze_activation does for inputs. ## Rip out Nothing yet. ## Check Unit tests in semantic.rs (or a sibling test module): (a) two publishers' contributions join by lub; (b) retracting one publisher recomputes the join and reports the key changed only if the aggregate moved; (c) extend never lowers a standing contribution; (d) empty join == RuntimeDemand::ignore (bottom). `cargo test --lib` green, zero warnings.
title: Runtime demand: ReturnDemand contribution store mirroring ActivationInputMap
